channel.description: Get up to speed on the news each morning with our daily radio show and podcast, “Marketplace Morning Report,” hosted by Kimberly Adams. We give you the economy without the anxiety, in the amount of time it takes to brew a cup of coffee. Start your day with us, on air or by downloading our podcast, for context and perspective on the economic news that matters to you.

item.title: Afghan refugees create their own food culture in Texas
item.itunes:author: Marketplace
item.description:
It’s been five years since tens of thousands of people were airlifted out of Afghanistan and brought to U.S. cities. Families arrived in chaotic conditions, but their arrival also sparked a wave of entrepreneurship. In Houston — which received more than 5,500 Afghans after the evacuation — new Afghan restaurants and grocery stores are part of a growing food scene. But first in this episode: new sanctions tied to the Nvidia scandal and a lookahead at the PCE price index.

item.title: Do you have flood insurance?
item.itunes:author: Marketplace
item.description:
As the climate changes, flooding is becoming more frequent and intense around the country. But while 90% of natural disasters in the U.S. involve flooding, just 6% of homeowners have flood insurance. Plus, accommodations for pregnant workers could be in jeopardy, and Erik Gordon, a business professor at the University of Michigan's Ross School of Business, shares his thoughts on Jensen Huang’s outsized role in our economy.

item.title: Jensen Huang is back
item.itunes:author: Marketplace
item.description:
The Nvidia board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO just days after he stepped down following revelations of multiple affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. A company press release also said the board received "input from senior levels of the United States government." We have the latest. Also in this episode: unpacking last week's stock sell-off and understanding the ripple effects of fewer professional book critics.

item.title: What to know about Medicaid work requirements
item.itunes:author: Marketplace
item.description:
Starting next year, roughly 20 million people will need to prove they’re working, volunteering, going to school, or have an exemption to keep their Medicaid. Republicans pushed through big changes to the program as part of President Donald Trump's tax and spending law from last year, including these so-called “work requirements.” Today, we dig into the timeline, how states are communicating changes, and more. But first: how energy prices are fueling global inflation.

item.title: What the Deutsche Bank leak reveals
item.itunes:author: Marketplace
item.description:
A new flood of leaked documents is putting fresh scrutiny on banking behemoth Deutsche Bank. The documents include more than 15 million internal emails and files, covering the early 2010s through 2021. A group of more than 200 journalists from around the globe has been analyzing the leaked information, revealing questionable practices, deals with Russian oligarchs, and more. Today, we hear from one of those reporters. But first, what did we get out of President Donald Trump's Asia summit?

item.title: Why JetBlue is in the red
item.itunes:author: Marketplace
item.description:
Last week’s nationwide FAA ground stoppage hit JetBlue particularly hard. No other airline canceled a higher percentage of its flights than JetBlue, according to The Wall Street Journal. The company was already under pressure from investors worried about its heavy debt load and its struggles to turn a profit. What is the path forward for JetBlue? But first, when it comes to Federal Reserve rate hikes, size really does matter.
